claim: Neuraminidase (NA) in H3N2 virus has evolved extensively for more than 50 years due to continuous immune pressure.
source: As one of the main influenza antigens, neuraminidase (NA) in H3N2 virus has evolved extensively for more than 50 years due to continuous immune pressure.
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing accumulation of mutations over time and is consistent with established knowledge about antigenic drift.

claim: NA has recently emerged as an effective vaccine target.
source: While NA has recently emerged as an effective vaccine target, biophysical constraints on the antigenic evolution of NA remain largely elusive.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent studies showing NA immunity's role in protection.

claim: The local fitness landscape of an NA antigenic region correlates well among six different H3N2 strains isolated around 10 years apart.
source: The local fitness landscape correlates well among strains and the pairwise epistasis is highly conserved.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from combinatorial mutagenesis and sequencing experiments showing Pearson correlations of 0.48-0.79 across genetic backgrounds.

claim: Local net charge governs the pairwise epistasis in the studied NA antigenic region.
source: Our analysis further demonstrates that local net charge governs the pairwise epistasis in this antigenic region.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that amino acid variants with opposite charges exhibit positive epistasis while variants with the same charge exhibit negative epistasis.

claim: Residue coevolution in the studied NA antigenic region is correlated with pairwise epistasis between charge states.
source: In addition, we show that residue coevolution in this antigenic region is correlated with the pairwise epistasis between charge states.
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis showing high correlation (Pearson correlation = 0.79-0.92) between coevolution scores and pairwise epistasis.

claim: NA immunity has a significant role in protection against influenza infection.
source: Although influenza vaccine development has traditionally focused on HA, NA has emerged as an effective vaccine target in the past few years because recent studies have shown that NA immunity has a significant role in protection against influenza infection (Monto et al., 2015; Weiss et al., 2020; Couch et al., 2013; Memoli et al., 2016; Krammer et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Influenza NA has an N-terminal transmembrane domain, a stalk domain, and a C-terminal head domain.
source: Influenza NA has an N-terminal transmembrane domain, a stalk domain, and a C-terminal head domain.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about influenza NA.

claim: The head domain of NA functions as an enzyme to cleave the host receptor (sialylated glycan), which is essential for virus release.
source: The head domain of NA functions as an enzyme to cleave the host receptor (i.e., sialylated glycan), which is essential for virus release.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NA enzymatic function.

claim: Most NA antibodies target the surface loop regions that surround the highly conserved catalytic active site.
source: Most NA antibodies target the surface loop regions that surround the highly conserved catalytic active site (Gulati et al., 2002; Malby et al., 1994; Venkatramani et al., 2006; Colman et al., 1983; Air, 2012; Zhu et al., 2019; Tulip et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published structural and immunological studies.

claim: Both HA and NA of human influenza virus have evolved extensively due to the need to constantly escape from herd immunity (antigenic drift).
source: Due to the need to constantly escape from herd immunity (also known as antigenic drift), both HA and NA of human influenza virus have evolved extensively (Kilbourne et al., 1990; Sandbulte et al., 2011; Westgeest et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and is consistent with established knowledge about influenza evolution.

claim: Since influenza H3N2 virus entered the human population in 1968, its HA has accumulated more than 83 amino acid mutations.
source: For example, since influenza H3N2 virus entered the human population in 1968, its HA and NA have accumulated more than 83 and 73 amino acid mutations, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which accounted for ~15% of their protein sequences.
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Since influenza H3N2 virus entered the human population in 1968, its NA has accumulated more than 73 amino acid mutations.
source: For example, since influenza H3N2 virus entered the human population in 1968, its HA and NA have accumulated more than 83 and 73 amino acid mutations, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which accounted for ~15% of their protein sequences.
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The accumulated mutations in HA and NA since 1968 accounted for approximately 15% of their protein sequences.
source: For example, since influenza H3N2 virus entered the human population in 1968, its HA and NA have accumulated more than 83 and 73 amino acid mutations, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which accounted for ~15% of their protein sequences.
evidence: This is calculated from the mutation data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The evolution of NA is much less well characterized as compared to HA.
source: However, the evolution of NA is much less well characterized as compared to HA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the state of the literature and research focus.

claim: Epistasis is a phenomenon in which the fitness effect of a mutation is dependent on the presence or absence of other mutations.
source: Epistasis is a phenomenon in which the fitness effect of a mutation is dependent on the presence or absence of other mutations.
evidence: This is a standard definition in evolutionary biology.

claim: Epistasis can lead to differential fitness effects of a given mutation on different genetic backgrounds.
source: Since epistasis can lead to differential fitness effects of a given mutation on different genetic backgrounds, it can restrict evolutionary trajectories or open up a new functional sequence space that would otherwise be inaccessible (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and represents established knowledge about epistasis.

claim: Epistasis can restrict evolutionary trajectories or open up a new functional sequence space that would otherwise be inaccessible.
source: Since epistasis can lead to differential fitness effects of a given mutation on different genetic backgrounds, it can restrict evolutionary trajectories or open up a new functional sequence space that would otherwise be inaccessible (Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and represents established knowledge about epistasis.

claim: Epistasis is a primary challenge for predicting evolution.
source: As a result, epistasis is a primary challenge for predicting evolution (Miton and Tokuriki, 2016; Luksza and Lässig, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work on evolutionary prediction.

claim: Epistasis is pervasive in natural evolution in general.
source: Nevertheless, epistasis is pervasive in natural evolution in general (Breen et al., 2012) and has been shown to influence the evolution of influenza virus (Gong et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2016; Lyons and Lauring, 2018; Wu et al., 2018; Kryazhimskiy et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2020; Koel et al., 2019; Bloom et al., 2010; Abed et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2013; Duan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Epistasis has been shown to influence the evolution of influenza virus.
source: Nevertheless, epistasis is pervasive in natural evolution in general (Breen et al., 2012) and has been shown to influence the evolution of influenza virus (Gong et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2016; Lyons and Lauring, 2018; Wu et al., 2018; Kryazhimskiy et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2020; Koel et al., 2019; Bloom et al., 2010; Abed et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2013; Duan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published work on influenza evolution.

claim: Epistasis is critical for the emergence of oseltamivir-resistant mutants of influenza NA.
source: While epistasis is critical for the emergence of oseltamivir-resistant mutants of influenza NA (Bloom et al., 2010; Abed et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2013; Duan et al., 2014), the role of epistasis and the underlying biophysical constraints on NA antigenic evolution remains largely unclear.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published work on drug resistance.

claim: The role of epistasis and the underlying biophysical constraints on NA antigenic evolution remains largely unclear.
source: While epistasis is critical for the emergence of oseltamivir-resistant mutants of influenza NA (Bloom et al., 2010; Abed et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2013; Duan et al., 2014), the role of epistasis and the underlying biophysical constraints on NA antigenic evolution remains largely unclear.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Deep mutational scanning combines saturation mutagenesis and next-generation sequencing to determine the phenotypic effects of numerous mutations in a highly parallel manner.
source: Deep mutational scanning combines saturation mutagenesis and next-generation sequencing to determine the phenotypic effects of numerous mutations in a highly parallel manner (Lee et al., 2018; Narayanan and Procko, 2021; Fowler and Fields, 2014).
evidence: This is a standard definition of deep mutational scanning supported by citations.

claim: Deep mutational scanning has been employed to measure the replication fitness effect of all possible single amino acid mutations across different influenza proteins.
source: Deep mutational scanning has been employed to measure the replication fitness effect of all possible single amino acid mutations across different influenza proteins (Lee et al., 2018; Thyagarajan and Bloom, 2014; Doud et al., 2015; Soh et al., 2019; Hom et al., 2019), which in turn can help to model the natural evolution of human influenza virus (Lee et al., 2018; Thyagarajan and Bloom, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published deep mutational scanning studies.

claim: Deep mutational scanning data can help to model the natural evolution of human influenza virus.
source: Deep mutational scanning has been employed to measure the replication fitness effect of all possible single amino acid mutations across different influenza proteins (Lee et al., 2018; Thyagarajan and Bloom, 2014; Doud et al., 2015; Soh et al., 2019; Hom et al., 2019), which in turn can help to model the natural evolution of human influenza virus (Lee et al., 2018; Thyagarajan and Bloom, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Most deep mutational scanning experiments lack the power to systematically measure the fitness of variants with two or more mutations.
source: However, most deep mutational scanning experiments lack the power to systematically measure the fitness of variants with two or more mutations, hence epistasis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the technical limitations of conventional deep mutational scanning approaches.

claim: Combinatorial mutagenesis was used in conjunction with next-generation sequencing to examine the local fitness landscape and to identify epistasis in influenza HA.
source: More recently, combinatorial mutagenesis was used in conjunction with next-generation sequencing to examine the local fitness landscape and to identify epistasis in influenza HA (Wu et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Combinatorial mutagenesis enables measurement of the fitness of high-order mutants.
source: Unlike saturation mutagenesis in conventional deep mutational scanning, combinatorial mutagenesis enables us to measure the fitness of high-order mutants.
evidence: This is a technical description of the capabilities of combinatorial mutagenesis.

claim: Studies dissecting the mechanistic basis of epistasis have provided important insight into the biophysical constraints on HA antigenic evolution.
source: By dissecting the mechanistic basis of epistasis, these studies have provided important insight into the biophysical constraints on HA antigenic evolution (Wu et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: When the structure of N2 NA was first reported in 1983, seven regions (I–VII) were proposed to be targeted by antibodies.
source: When the structure of N2 NA was first reported in 1983 (Varghese et al., 1983), seven regions (I–VII) were proposed to be targeted by antibodies (Colman et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the original structural studies.

claim: Within regions I–III of NA, mutations at residues 329, 344, 368, and 370 have been shown to escape monoclonal antibodies.
source: Within regions I–III, mutations at residues 329, 344, 368, and 370 have been shown to escape monoclonal antibodies (Gulati et al., 2002; Varghese et al., 1988; Air et al., 1985).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published antibody escape studies.

claim: Residues 328, 329, 344, 367, 368, 369, and 370 form a cluster of seven residues that are very close in space.
source: These four residues, along with residues 328 (region I), 367 (region III), and 369 (region III), form a cluster of seven residues that are very close in space (Figure 1a and b).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1a and b.

claim: Residues 328 and 367 are under positive selection in human H3N2 NA.
source: Both residues 328 and 367 are under positive selection in human H3N2 NA (Westgeest et al., 2012), whereas coevolution of residues 367 and 369 in human H3N2 NA has created an N-glycosylation site (NXT) at residue 367 during 2010 (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published selection analysis study.

claim: Coevolution of residues 367 and 369 in human H3N2 NA has created an N-glycosylation site (NXT) at residue 367 during 2010.
source: Both residues 328 and 367 are under positive selection in human H3N2 NA (Westgeest et al., 2012), whereas coevolution of residues 367 and 369 in human H3N2 NA has created an N-glycosylation site (NXT) at residue 367 during 2010 (Figure 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Residues 328, 367, and 369 participated in the antigenic drift of human H3N2 NA.
source: These observations indicate that residues 328, 367, and 369 also participated in the antigenic drift of human H3N2 NA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the positive selection and coevolution data.

claim: Only 53 of the 864 possible haplotypes of interest have been observed in naturally circulating human H3N2 strains.
source: Together, there are 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 2 × 4 × 2 = 864 possible amino acid combinations (also called haplotypes) across these seven residues, although only 53 of them have been observed in naturally circulating human H3N2 strains (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The six strains studied (HK68, Bk79, Bei89, Mos99, Vic11, and HK19) were all historical vaccine strains isolated approximately 10 years apart.
source: All these six strains were historical vaccine strains and isolated approximately 10 years apart.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the strains used in the study.

claim: A high correlation was observed between biological replicates of the fitness measurements (Pearson correlation = 0.81–0.89) except for HK68 and Bk79 (0.39 and 0.63, respectively).
source: Overall, a high correlation was observed between the replicates (Pearson correlation = 0.81–0.89) except for HK68 and Bk79 (0.39 and 0.63, respectively), mostly due to the high measurement noise for low fitness variants (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The lower correlation for HK68 and Bk79 replicates was mostly due to high measurement noise for low fitness variants.
source: Overall, a high correlation was observed between the replicates (Pearson correlation = 0.81–0.89) except for HK68 and Bk79 (0.39 and 0.63, respectively), mostly due to the high measurement noise for low fitness variants (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an inference based on the data patterns shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Most variants were strongly deleterious (fitness < -1) in HK68.
source: Interestingly, while most variants were strongly deleterious (i.e., had a fitness of <-1) in HK68, variants with a fitness of <-1 were rare in other genetic backgrounds (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Variants with fitness < -1 were rare in genetic backgrounds other than HK68.
source: Interestingly, while most variants were strongly deleterious (i.e., had a fitness of <-1) in HK68, variants with a fitness of <-1 were rare in other genetic backgrounds (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The difference in variant fitness distribution across genetic backgrounds was not due to the difference in their WT replication fitness.
source: Notably, the difference in variant fitness distribution across genetic backgrounds was not due to the difference in their WT replication fitness since the viral titers from a rescue experiment were similar among HK68 WT, Bei89 WT, and Mos99 WT (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The fitness of individual variants correlated well across genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.48–0.79).
source: In contrast, the fitness of individual variants correlated well across genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.48–0.79, Figure 2b), despite their differences in variant absolute fitness values (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Epistasis exists between the seven-residue antigenic region and the rest of the NA sequence, but such epistasis is largely variant-nonspecific.
source: These results demonstrate that although epistasis exists between the seven-residue antigenic region and the rest of the NA sequence, such epistasis is largely variant-nonspecific.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that fitness correlates well across backgrounds despite differences in absolute values.

claim: The topology of the local fitness landscape is highly conserved across genetic backgrounds.
source: Consequently, the topology of the local fitness landscape is highly conserved across genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high correlation of variant fitness across backgrounds.

claim: The observation of conserved fitness landscape topology in NA is very different from a similar study on a major antigenic site of HA, where the topology differed dramatically among genetic backgrounds.
source: This observation is very different from a similar study on a major antigenic site of HA, where the topology of the local fitness landscape differed dramatically among genetic backgrounds (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published study on HA.

claim: Most natural variants have a fitness between –0.5 and 0.5 on the background of Bk79, Bei89, Mos99, Vic11, and HK19.
source: Most natural variants have a fitness between –0.5 and 0.5 on the background of Bk79, Bei89, Mos99, Vic11, and HK19.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Most natural variants from 1980s onward are strongly deleterious with fitness <-1 on the background of HK68.
source: In contrast, most natural variants from 1980s onward are strongly deleterious with fitness <-1 on the background of HK68, indicating many natural variants would not have emerged if the genetic background had not evolved.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Many natural variants would not have emerged if the genetic background had not evolved.
source: In contrast, most natural variants from 1980s onward are strongly deleterious with fitness <-1 on the background of HK68, indicating many natural variants would not have emerged if the genetic background had not evolved.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that later variants are deleterious on the HK68 background.

claim: The emergence of natural variants in the antigenic region of interest is contingent on the evolution of the rest of the NA sequence.
source: In other words, the emergence of natural variants in the antigenic region of interest is contingent on the evolution of the rest of the NA sequence.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that variants have different fitness on different genetic backgrounds.

claim: HK68 has a much lower mutational tolerance at the studied antigenic region compared to other strains.
source: This result is consistent with the observation that HK68 has a much lower mutational tolerance at this antigenic region (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The correlations between additive fitness contributions varied hugely across genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.12–0.88).
source: While the correlations between additive fitness contributions varied hugely across genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.12–0.88, Figure 3a and c, Figure 3—figure supplement 2), we observed generally strong correlations between pairwise epistatic effects across the six different genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.69–0.86, Figure 3b and c, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3a, c, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Generally strong correlations were observed between pairwise epistatic effects across the six different genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.69–0.86).
source: While the correlations between additive fitness contributions varied hugely across genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.12–0.88, Figure 3a and c, Figure 3—figure supplement 2), we observed generally strong correlations between pairwise epistatic effects across the six different genetic backgrounds (Pearson correlation = 0.69–0.86, Figure 3b and c, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3b, c, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The variation of additive fitness contributions across genetic backgrounds does not strictly depend on the similarity between genetic backgrounds.
source: Of note, the variation of additive fitness contributions across genetic backgrounds does not seem to strictly depend on the similarity between genetic backgrounds since the correlation between the additive fitness contributions of HK68 and HK19 (Pearson correlation = 0.46) is much higher than that of HK68 and Bk79 (Pearson correlation = 0.12), which have a shorter time separation.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing correlations between strains with different time separations.

claim: The observation of variable additive fitness but conserved epistasis points at a possibility for complex epistatic interactions between the antigenic region of interest and other regions on NA.
source: This observation points at a possibility for complex epistatic interactions between the antigenic region of interest and other regions on NA.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed patterns of additive fitness variation.

claim: Pairwise epistasis, but not additive fitness, is highly conserved at the NA antigenic region of interest across genetic backgrounds.
source: Overall, these results indicate that pairwise epistasis, but not additive fitness, is highly conserved at the NA antigenic region of interest across genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the data showing high correlation for epistasis but not for additive fitness.

claim: An 'additive-only' model without accounting for epistasis shows a poor fit to the fitness landscape data compared to the model with epistasis.
source: Consistently, an 'additive-only' model, without accounting for epistasis, shows a poor fit to the fitness landscape data compared to the model above with epistasis (Figure 3—figure supplement 4a), despite the fact that the inferred additive fitness effects correlate well between the two models (Figure 3—figure supplement 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by model comparison data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4a.

claim: The inferred additive fitness effects correlate well between the additive-only model and the pairwise epistasis model.
source: Consistently, an 'additive-only' model, without accounting for epistasis, shows a poor fit to the fitness landscape data compared to the model above with epistasis (Figure 3—figure supplement 4a), despite the fact that the inferred additive fitness effects correlate well between the two models (Figure 3—figure supplement 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4b.

claim: Amino acid variants with opposite charges usually exhibited positive epistasis.
source: We noticed that amino acid variants with opposite charges usually exhibited positive epistasis, whereas amino acid variants with the same charge usually exhibited negative epistasis (Figures 3b and 4a, Figure 3—figure supplement 5, Figure 4—figure supplement 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Amino acid variants with the same charge usually exhibited negative epistasis.
source: We noticed that amino acid variants with opposite charges usually exhibited positive epistasis, whereas amino acid variants with the same charge usually exhibited negative epistasis (Figures 3b and 4a, Figure 3—figure supplement 5, Figure 4—figure supplement 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Pairwise interactions that involved a neutral amino acid variant did not show any bias towards positive or negative epistasis.
source: In contrast, pairwise interactions that involved a neutral amino acid variant did not show any bias towards positive or negative epistasis.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis.

claim: Balancing of charged amino acid variants imposes a key biophysical constraint on the evolution of the studied NA antigenic region.
source: These results suggest that balancing of charged amino acid variants imposes a key biophysical constraint on the evolution of this NA antigenic region.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed patterns of epistasis related to charge.

claim: The distance between the side-chain carboxylate oxygen of E344 and the side-chain amine nitrogen of K369 is 6.6 Å.
source: Our structural analysis showed that the distance between the side-chain carboxylate oxygen of E344 and the side-chain amine nitrogen of K369 is 6.6 Å, whereas the distance between the side-chain carboxylate oxygen of E344 and the side-chain amine nitrogen of K328 is 5.5 Å (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The distance between the side-chain carboxylate oxygen of E344 and the side-chain amine nitrogen of K328 is 5.5 Å.
source: Our structural analysis showed that the distance between the side-chain carboxylate oxygen of E344 and the side-chain amine nitrogen of K369 is 6.6 Å, whereas the distance between the side-chain carboxylate oxygen of E344 and the side-chain amine nitrogen of K328 is 5.5 Å (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: At distances of 5.5-6.6 Å, salt bridges cannot be formed and the electrostatic attraction force is negligible.
source: At these distances, salt bridges cannot be formed and the electrostatic attraction force is negligible (Kumar and Nussinov, 2002; Shashikala et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work on salt bridge formation.

claim: The distance between the side-chain amine nitrogen atoms of K328 and K369 is 11.6 Å.
source: Similarly, the distance between the side-chain amine nitrogen atoms of K328 and K369 is 11.6 Å (Figure 4b), which is too far for any significant electrostatic repulsion force (Shashikala et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: A distance of 11.6 Å is too far for any significant electrostatic repulsion force.
source: Similarly, the distance between the side-chain amine nitrogen atoms of K328 and K369 is 11.6 Å (Figure 4b), which is too far for any significant electrostatic repulsion force (Shashikala et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to published work on electrostatic interactions.

claim: Direct side-chain–side-chain interaction via electrostatic attraction or repulsion is unlikely to be a major determinant for epistasis in the studied NA antigenic region.
source: As a result, direct side-chain–side-chain interaction via electrostatic attraction or repulsion is unlikely to be a major determinant for epistasis in this NA antigenic region.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural distance measurements.

claim: Pairwise epistasis between two amino acid variants does not correlate with their side-chain–side-chain distances.
source: Consistently, pairwise epistasis between two amino acid variants does not correlate with their side-chain–side-chain distances (Figure 4d–f, Figure 4—figure supplement 3), further substantiating that direct side-chain–side-chain interaction is not a determinant for epistasis here.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4d-f and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Variants tended to have a higher fitness when the local net charge was around –1.
source: In all genetic backgrounds, variants tended to have a higher fitness when the local net charge was around –1, while variants with a more positive or negative local net charge usually had a lower fitness (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Variants with a more positive or negative local net charge usually had a lower fitness.
source: In all genetic backgrounds, variants tended to have a higher fitness when the local net charge was around –1, while variants with a more positive or negative local net charge usually had a lower fitness (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The local net charge is a key molecular phenotype with a biophysical function that is under balancing selection.
source: Overall, our results demonstrate that the local net charge is a key molecular phenotype with a biophysical function that is under balancing selection.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that intermediate charge values have higher fitness.

claim: The local net charge biophysical phenotype imposes a strong constraint on the evolution of the NA antigenic region, reflected in the conserved epistatic interactions between amino acid variants.
source: This biophysical phenotype imposes a strong constraint on the evolution of the NA antigenic region, reflected in the conserved epistatic interactions between amino acid variants of this region.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed relationship between charge and epistasis.

claim: Most natural variants in the antigenic region of interest had a local net charge between –1 and +1.
source: Most natural variants in the antigenic region of interest had a local net charge between –1 and +1 (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Natural variants with a local net charge of −3, –2, +2, or +3 could be observed but were rare.
source: Natural variants with a local net charge of −3,–2, + 2, or +3 could also be observed but were rare.
evidence: This is an observation from the natural sequence data analysis.

claim: The natural evolution of the studied NA antigenic region is constrained by balancing the local net charge.
source: This observation suggests that the natural evolution of this NA antigenic region is constrained by balancing the local net charge.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most natural variants have intermediate charge values.

claim: High correlation was observed between coevolution score and pairwise epistasis (Pearson correlation = 0.79–0.92).
source: When we compared the coevolution score with the pairwise epistasis (Figure 5c, Figure 5—figure supplement 4), high correlation was observed (Pearson correlation = 0.79–0.92).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5c and Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: Pairs of charge states with opposite charges usually have positive coevolution scores and positive epistasis.
source: Specifically, pairs with opposite charges usually have positive coevolution scores and positive epistasis, whereas pairs with the same charge usually have negative coevolution scores and negative epistasis.
evidence: This is an observation from the coevolution and epistasis analysis.

claim: Pairs of charge states with the same charge usually have negative coevolution scores and negative epistasis.
source: Specifically, pairs with opposite charges usually have positive coevolution scores and positive epistasis, whereas pairs with the same charge usually have negative coevolution scores and negative epistasis.
evidence: This is an observation from the coevolution and epistasis analysis.

claim: The realized evolutionary trajectories in nature are seldom the most probable ones among an ensemble of trajectories constructed from the fitness data.
source: Nonetheless, the realized evolutionary trajectories in nature are seldom the most probable ones among an ensemble of trajectories that were constructed from the fitness data (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: A biophysically grounded epistatic landscape is correlated with the natural coevolution of residues in the studied NA antigenic region.
source: As a result, while our analysis demonstrates that a biophysically grounded epistatic landscape is correlated with the natural coevolution of residues in this NA antigenic region, additional considerations are needed for the prediction of the exact amino acid mutations along the evolutionary trajectory.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the correlation between epistasis and coevolution.

claim: Additional considerations beyond fitness and epistasis are needed for the prediction of the exact amino acid mutations along the evolutionary trajectory.
source: As a result, while our analysis demonstrates that a biophysically grounded epistatic landscape is correlated with the natural coevolution of residues in this NA antigenic region, additional considerations are needed for the prediction of the exact amino acid mutations along the evolutionary trajectory.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that fitness-based trajectories don't match realized trajectories.

claim: Understanding the biophysical constraints is a key to model the molecular evolution of proteins.
source: Understanding the biophysical constraints is a key to model the molecular evolution of proteins (Echave and Wilke, 2017; Luksza and Lässig, 2014; Nourmohammad et al., 2013; Otwinowski et al., 2018; Mustonen et al., 2008; Wylie and Shakhnovich, 2011; Lässig et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published work on protein evolution modeling.

claim: The local net charge is a major biophysical molecular phenotype that constrains the evolution of an antigenic region in human influenza H3N2 NA.
source: Through a systematic analysis of pairwise epistasis, this study shows that the local net charge is a major biophysical molecular phenotype that constrains the evolution of an antigenic region in human influenza H3N2 NA.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding supported by the experimental data.

claim: Pairwise epistasis is highly conserved across diverse genetic backgrounds in the studied NA antigenic region.
source: An important feature for this antigenic region of interest is that pairwise epistasis is highly conserved across diverse genetic backgrounds, which in turn is correlated with residue coevolution in naturally circulating human influenza H3N2 virus.
evidence: This is a summary of findings supported by the experimental data.

claim: Pairwise epistasis is correlated with residue coevolution in naturally circulating human influenza H3N2 virus.

claim: The homologous regions in the H1N1 NA and influenza B NA do not evolve as extensively as human influenza H3N2 NA.
source: Although the homologous regions in the H1N1 NA and influenza B NA do not evolve as extensively as human influenza H3N2 NA (Figure 5—figure supplement 6), residue 329 coevolves with 344 in seasonal influenza H1N1 NA, indicating that similar local net charge balancing may also influence the evolution of H1N1 NA.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6.

claim: Residue 329 coevolves with 344 in seasonal influenza H1N1 NA.
source: Although the homologous regions in the H1N1 NA and influenza B NA do not evolve as extensively as human influenza H3N2 NA (Figure 5—figure supplement 6), residue 329 coevolves with 344 in seasonal influenza H1N1 NA, indicating that similar local net charge balancing may also influence the evolution of H1N1 NA.

claim: Similar local net charge balancing may also influence the evolution of H1N1 NA.
source: Although the homologous regions in the H1N1 NA and influenza B NA do not evolve as extensively as human influenza H3N2 NA (Figure 5—figure supplement 6), residue 329 coevolves with 344 in seasonal influenza H1N1 NA, indicating that similar local net charge balancing may also influence the evolution of H1N1 NA.

claim: Earlier theoretical studies have indicated that charge balancing is one of the strongest signatures of correlated evolution across different protein families.
source: In fact, earlier theoretical studies have indicated that charge balancing is one of the strongest signatures of correlated evolution across different protein families (Neher, 1994; Magliery and Regan, 2004; Callahan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published theoretical work.

claim: This study provides empirical evidence for charge balancing as a signature of correlated evolution.
source: Our study here further provided empirical evidence for this phenomenon.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the current study.

claim: The optimal local net charge at the antigenic region of interest is slightly negative.
source: A key finding of this study is that the optimal local net charge at the antigenic region of interest is slightly negative, and an increase or decrease in local net charge is deleterious.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the fitness data.

claim: An increase or decrease in local net charge from the optimal value is deleterious.
source: A key finding of this study is that the optimal local net charge at the antigenic region of interest is slightly negative, and an increase or decrease in local net charge is deleterious.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the fitness data.

claim: The local net charge may be the key molecular phenotype under stabilizing and balancing selection.
source: This characteristic suggests that the local net charge may be the key molecular phenotype under stabilizing and balancing selection, imposing a biophysical constraint on evolution of the NA antigenic region.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of optimal intermediate charge values.

claim: The local net charge may affect the kinetics of host membrane attachment and virus release because the host cell membrane and sialylated glycan receptor are both negatively charged.
source: First, since the host cell membrane and sialylated glycan receptor are both negatively charged, charge distribution on the virus surface, including the antigenic region of interest, may affect the kinetics of host membrane attachment and virus release.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional role of local net charge.

claim: The local net charge may affect the catalytic efficiency of NA because the antigenic region of interest is proximal to the catalytic active site.
source: Second, the antigenic region of interest is proximal to the catalytic active site (Figure 1a), the local net charge may affect the catalytic efficiency of NA.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional role of local net charge.

claim: The local net charge may influence the protein stability of NA.
source: Lastly, the local net charge may influence the protein stability of NA (de Graff et al., 2016; Raghunathan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to published work on protein stability.

claim: The ancestral strain HK68 has a much lower mutational tolerance at the antigenic region of interest than the subsequent strains.
source: One interesting observation in this study is that the ancestral strain HK68 has a much lower mutational tolerance at the antigenic region of interest than the subsequent strains, although the topology of the local fitness landscapes is largely conserved across strains.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the fitness data.

claim: Other biophysical features of NA are evolving over time and epistatically interact with the antigenic region of interest in a residue nonspecific manner.
source: This result suggests that other biophysical features of NA are evolving over time and that they epistatically interact with the antigenic region of interest in a residue nonspecific manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of different mutational tolerance across strains.

claim: Nonspecific epistasis is often related to protein stability.
source: Nonspecific epistasis is often related to protein stability (Starr and Thornton, 2016), which is best described by the threshold robustness model (Bloom et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Under the threshold robustness model, slightly destabilizing mutations may have neutral fitness when the protein has an excess stability margin but are deleterious when the protein is marginally stable.
source: Under the threshold robustness model, slightly destabilizing mutations may have neutral fitness when the protein has an excess stability margin but are deleterious when the protein is marginally stable.
evidence: This is an explanation of the threshold robustness model from established knowledge.

claim: The threshold robustness model can be used to explain the differential variant fitness distribution among the six genetic backgrounds.
source: Threshold robustness model can be used to explain the differential variant fitness distribution among the six genetic backgrounds in our study.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed fitness differences.

claim: Mos99 NA may have an excess stability margin such that many variants are nearly neutral despite being slightly destabilizing.
source: For example, it is possible that Mos99 NA has an excess stability margin such that many variants are nearly neutral despite being slightly destabilizing.
evidence: This is speculation about the stability of Mos99 NA.

claim: The same slightly destabilizing variants that are nearly neutral in Mos99 are highly deleterious in HK68 NA because it is marginally stable.
source: In contrast, the same slightly destabilizing variants are highly deleterious in HK68 NA because it is marginally stable.
evidence: This is speculation about the stability of HK68 NA.

claim: Some nonlinearity can be observed when comparing variant fitness in different genetic backgrounds, which is a feature of the threshold robustness model.
source: When comparing the variant fitness in different genetic backgrounds, some nonlinearity can be observed (Figure 2b), which is a feature of the threshold robustness model (Otwinowski et al., 2018; Bloom Jesse et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an observation from the data supported by citations.

claim: Additional studies are needed to confirm whether the difference in variant fitness distribution among genetic backgrounds is due to protein stability or other biophysical factors.
source: Nevertheless, additional studies are needed to confirm whether the difference in variant fitness distribution among genetic backgrounds is due to protein stability or other biophysical factors.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study.

claim: Predicting the evolution of human influenza virus is a challenging task, yet important for seasonal influenza vaccine development.
source: Predicting the evolution of human influenza virus is a challenging task, yet important for seasonal influenza vaccine development.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance and difficulty of influenza evolution prediction.

claim: An accurate predictive model of human influenza evolution likely requires an integration of epitope information, antigenic data, mutant fitness measurement, and experimental selection for antibody escape variants.
source: An accurate predictive model of human influenza evolution likely requires an integration of epitope information (Luksza and Lässig, 2014), antigenic data (Neher et al., 2016), mutant fitness measurement (Lee et al., 2018), and experimental selection for antibody escape variants (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published work on influenza evolution prediction.

claim: A biophysical epistatic model of antigenic fitness landscape can be instrumental in modeling the evolution of human influenza virus.
source: This work further suggests that a biophysical epistatic model of antigenic fitness landscape can also be instrumental in modeling the evolution of human influenza virus.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of the current study.

claim: A unifying model that can accurately predict emerging mutations may one day be built as knowledge about the evolutionary biology of influenza virus accumulates.
source: As the knowledge about the evolutionary biology of influenza virus accumulates, a unifying model that can accurately predict emerging mutation may one day be built.
evidence: This is speculation about future developments in the field.
